methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1.1B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 9 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

data.narrative:
Walden Robotics is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company led by founder Russ Tedrake, former SVP of Large Behavior Models at Toyota Research Institute. The company carries a last post-money valuation of $1.1B against $300M total raised. The valuation peer set comprises nine same-sector comparables at similar valuation tiers, including eight private companies (Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics among them) and one public company.

Two quantitative methods anchor the analysis. Stage-progression modeling applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $1.1B base, implying $2.8B. Peer-median analysis across the nine-company set yields a $1.8B median valuation, with a range spanning $1.0B to $2.3B. These approaches triangulate to a low-to-high range of $1.5B to $3.2B, with a median of $2.2B.

Key uncertainties include execution risk typical of seed-stage deployment and the concentration of the peer set in relatively mature funding stages (Series B through F), which may overweight later-stage multiples. The current $1.1B valuation sits below both the peer median and the triangulated midpoint, suggesting either below-market positioning or material founder/technical strength premia not yet reflected in valuation. The analysis supports a range of $1.5B to $3.2B, with $2.2B as the central estimate.
